title: Helpdesk forwards requests and replies without ctx.notify
detail: Forwarding a request, the reply mail dispatch and the in-app note are plain dispatches and now run through runBestEffort instead of the notify-gated sendBestEffort, so they no longer get skipped when the delivery feature is not mounted. The legacy contact subject lookup checks the archive first and decrypts an email only for anonymous requests.

title: Legacy contact data is exported, erased and expired from the event log
detail: The user-data hooks for requests stored under the former contact names read the dropped `read_contact_requests` and `read_contact_replies` tables, so the export failed and the forget run reported an error on an app that never had those tables. They now fold the `contact-request` and `contact-reply` event streams instead: the export lists the requests of the user (by user id, or by verified email for anonymous ones) with their replies, the forget run purges attachments, erases the record keys and archives the streams. A new maintenance job `helpdesk:job:legacy-contact-retention` applies the retention period to old legacy requests and replies. Deleting a user also erases the notes written on their helpdesk requests and legacy requests.

title: HELPDESK_REQUEST_ENTITY is exported from the helpdesk entry
detail: `HELPDESK_REQUEST_ENTITY` comes from `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-bundled-features/helpdesk` next to the other helpdesk constants.

title: Indexes for helpdesk requests and replies
detail: All helpdesk rows live in the system tenant, so the tenant index selected nothing. `read_helpdesk_requests` gets indexes on (tenant_id, status) and (tenant_id, reporter_user_id), `read_helpdesk_replies` on (tenant_id, request_id).
migration: Run `bun kumiko-schema generate` in the app to pick up the new indexes.

title: Helpdesk reply error passthrough, paged user-data lookups
detail: helpdesk reply returns the file takeover failure as is (file_rejected) instead of mapping everything to helpdesk_attachment_not_found, which is removed from HelpdeskErrors; user-data forget and export page through all requests and replies, the reply detail lists all replies; the exported SYSTEM_ADMIN_ROLE constant is removed and SystemAdmin checks use ROLES.SystemAdmin.
migration: Replace imports of SYSTEM_ADMIN_ROLE by ROLES.SystemAdmin; clients matching the helpdesk reply error helpdesk_attachment_not_found match file_rejected instead.

title: Public handlers declare only the anonymous role
detail: Handlers declaring access.anySignedIn next to the anonymous role list only anonymous in roles (the dropped signed-in roles never had an effect); the SUBMIT_ROLES constant of helpdesk is removed.

title: Notification preferences and config values of the former contact feature are carried over
detail: The helpdesk notifications declare `renamedFrom: ["contact:notify:<name>"]`, so stored preferences and address opt-outs under the former names keep applying (a helpdesk-name row wins). The boot job `helpdesk:job:legacy-contact-config` (`runOnBoot`, idempotent) writes `contact:config:reply-to` and `contact:config:telegram-chat` to `helpdesk:config:reply-to` and `helpdesk:config:telegram-chat` through `config:write:set` as SystemAdmin, only when the helpdesk key has no value yet; the old rows stay untouched. The job declares an `escapeHatch` (crossTenantReads, systemIdentity). This replaces the "not carried over" hint of the 0.413.0 migration note for these settings.

title: pre-rename contact requests are exported and erased with the user
detail: Since the rename from contact to helpdesk, requests and replies stored under the aggregates `contact-request` and `contact-reply` (tables `read_contact_requests`, `read_contact_replies`, attachments with that entity type) sat inert; the EXT_USER_DATA hooks only covered `helpdesk-*`, so a user's export missed them and an erasure left the personal data behind. The helpdesk feature now registers export and delete hooks for the former aggregate, matching by reporter user id or verified email like the current hooks. Deleting forgets the rows through the event-store executor, removes their attachments and shreds the record subject keys. The former entities are not registered, so no schema is generated for them, and installs without former data skip the hooks. The data-retention job does not see these rows, since it only walks registered entities.

title: acknowledgedSystemDb for system-scoped features
detail: `acknowledgedSystemDb(ctx, featureName, crossTenantReason)` returns `ctx.systemDb.acknowledgeCrossTenant(reason)` and throws an InternalError naming the feature when `r.systemScope()` is missing. helpdesk and waitlist use it, together with the shared `sendBestEffort` and `resolveVerifiedUserEmail`; behaviour and log texts are unchanged.

title: helpdesk sample: complete same-origin contact page
detail: `samples/apps/use-all-bundled/public/helpdesk-contact.html` (with `.js` and `.css`) loads `/helpdesk/client.js`, builds the form from `load()` (kinds, optional phone), submits with proof of work and a hidden honeypot field and shows the sent, rate-limited and failed states. Two Playwright specs cover a real submit that reaches the SystemAdmin inbox and a honeypot submit that stores nothing.

title: helpdesk recipe: client script same-origin, notes-history listed as required
detail: The recipe comment embedded `/helpdesk/client.js` from another origin, but the client posts to the relative paths `/api/query` and `/api/write` without cookies, so the page has to share the app's origin or forward `/api` to the app on its own origin. The recipe and its README now say so and list `notes-history` with `config`, `delivery`, `user-data-rights` and `files` as required features.

title: contact feature renamed to helpdesk
migration: The bundled feature contact is renamed to helpdesk; nothing keeps the old names. Imports: @cosmicdrift/kumiko-bundled-features/contact, /contact/web and /contact/client become /helpdesk, /helpdesk/web and /helpdesk/client; createContactFeature, contactOpenRequestsPanels, ContactOptions and the other Contact*/CONTACT_* exports become Helpdesk*/HELPDESK_* (createHelpdeskFeature, helpdeskOpenRequestsPanels, HelpdeskOptions). The feature name, handler, screen, config and i18n keys move from contact: to helpdesk:, the entities from contact-request/contact-reply to helpdesk-request/helpdesk-reply with the tables read_helpdesk_requests/read_helpdesk_replies, and error codes from contact_* to helpdesk_*. The browser client is served at GET /helpdesk/client.js and registers window.KumikoHelpdesk; update script tags, same-origin ingress paths and nav/legal references to the feature name. Notification preferences and opt-outs stored under contact:notify: are not carried over; the six notifications start with their defaults. Run kumiko schema generate and commit the migration. Data stored under the old names is not carried over: requests, replies and their events stay inert under contact-request/contact-reply, and the config values contact:config:reply-to and contact:config:telegram-chat are not read any more. Close open requests before upgrading and set reply-to and the Telegram chat again on the forwarding screen.

title: contact/client subpath, app name in the report hint, Telegram documented as optional
detail: `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-bundled-features/contact/client` exports `CONTACT_CLIENT_SOURCE` and the website client types `ContactWebsiteClient`, `ContactWebsiteWindow`, `ContactWebsiteSubmitFields`, `ContactWebsiteSubmitResult`, `ContactWebsiteFormOptions` and `ContactWebsiteKind`. The report form hint reads "Goes straight to the {appName} team" with the `appName` option (de, en, es, fr, it). With the default `telegram: false` the feature lists `channel-telegram` as an optional dependency only; the feature manifest, the recipe and the docs no longer show the Telegram config key or `contact:write:send-test` for that default. A signed-in visitor with any role can submit the website form and fetch the challenge.

title: New bundled feature contact: public contact form with spam protection, admin replies and Telegram forwarding
detail: `createContactFeature({ appName, telegram? })` adds a public contact form backend: the anonymous `contact:write:submit` stores a question, contact request or problem report (honeypot, single-use proof-of-work challenge from `contact:query:challenge`, minimum submit time, per-IP and per-email rate limits; spam gets the same 200 body and nothing is stored), notifies every SystemAdmin by mail and, with option `telegram: true` (default off), in a Telegram chat (adds `channel-telegram` to `requires`, the `telegramChat` config key and `contact:write:send-test`). The notification carries no personal data on any channel: only the kind, the app name and a link into the inbox, never name, address, phone, subject or message, because mail and Telegram cannot be shredded. A website sender gets a fixed acknowledgement that repeats nothing they typed (the form is no mail relay); a signed-in admin report gets a copy. The per-email limit counts only submits that passed the spam checks, `contact:write:report` is limited to 10 per hour and user, and the stored `page` loses its query string and fragment. Phone is off by default (`fields.phone`). Logged-in users file reports with `contact:write:report`; SystemAdmins answer with `contact:write:reply` (mail with Reply-To, optional in-app notice for logged-in reporters), mark requests done, and read `contact:query:request-detail`, `contact:query:replies` and `contact:query:request-delivery` (one row per channel with recipient, time and status email|telegram|reply-email|reply-in-app: pending|delivered|failed|skipped|read). Open means no answer yet: only status `open` counts. The browser client is served at `GET /contact/client.js` (`window.KumikoContact`). Requests are crypto-shredding-ready PII with EXT_USER_DATA export and erasure and a 365 day retention. The feature requires `config`, `delivery`, `user-data-rights` and `files` (a file provider must be mounted).
migration: Run `kumiko schema generate`: it adds the `contact-request` and `contact-reply` tables. Apps mounting contact also need the delivery and channel-in-app migrations (`idempotency_key` columns) and a mounted file provider.

title: contact option reportCancelTarget
detail: `createContactFeature({ reportCancelTarget })` sets the screen the Cancel button of the report form navigates to; without it the form shows no Cancel button.

title: contact option detailLinks; every signed-in user may report a problem
detail: `createContactFeature({ detailLinks: { user, tenant } })` sets the screens the sender and tenant links in the request detail header open (short id or `<feature>:screen:<id>`); defaults stay `user-edit` and `tenant-edit`, `false` removes a link. `contact:write:report` and the report screen are now open to every signed-in user (`openToAll`), not only TenantAdmin and Member. The detail layout drops the phone row while `fields.phone` is off and hides it for an empty value, and the contact feature now requires `notes-history` (the detail notes section needs it).

title: The contact website client sends without credentials
detail: `GET /contact/client.js` now sends the challenge and submit requests with `credentials: "omit"`, so a visitor who is signed in on the same domain with any role (including app roles) still submits as an anonymous caller instead of getting 403. Name and email come from the form, never from the session.
